Probably the one thing that is commonly overlooked is room acoustics and monitor setup. The better your room and monitors sound, the easier it is to dial in your recordings. Head over to Gearslutz and check out their Studio Building/Acoustics forum. Everything you need to know is there.

https://www.gearslutz.com/board/studio-building-acoustics/

One warning. Many of those guys are obsessed with getting perfect numbers on their rooms - and this is a deep and winding rabbit hole. For me "perfect" is less important than finding out your room and monitor weaknesses. Instead of getting things perfect, shoot for "pretty close".

If you are handy, you can build acoustic panels for fairly cheap. Mine are basically wood frames made from 1x4, stuffed with Roxul insulation, and covered with fabric I found on the budget table at Fabricland. Each 1'x4' panel probably only cost $15. You can see them on the ceiling of my last studio here. Those pictures were taken right after I got the equipment in the new space. I continued to do acoustic tests and ended up needing a few more panels on the walls. It wasn't perfect, but it was pretty damn close. Music sounded amazing in that room.
